frontend_notes_on_api_constraints: No route should imply binary file upload/download because the API explicitly excludes raw binary storage; use metadata/text/source URI registration language throughout the UI.

No page should promise automatic benchmark execution across Elastic/OpenSearch/Qdrant because the API only exposes MongoDB-side search execution plus generic query_result persistence. Side-by-side benchmark screens are read/write for stored results, not orchestrators for external systems.
No dedicated delete screens/actions should be included because delete endpoints are not part of the API contract.
No authentication, authorization admin, or agent session management screens should be invented because the API contract explicitly excludes them.
Ground-truth chunk selection is partially constrained: chunk browsing is available only per document and chunk profile via getDocumentChunksByProfile, not as a benchmark-wide chunk search experience.
Reranking can be displayed only if rerank_score is present in persisted query_results; there is no standalone rerank execution endpoint.
Because there is no endpoint to list query_results directly, benchmark analysis screens must rely on the provided summary, wins, and query comparison endpoints rather than an all-results browser.

BO-1.description: Evaluate AI capabilities that combine structured and unstructured data.

BO-2.description: Find a scalable lower-cost solution for unstructured or hybrid structured/unstructured retrieval workloads.

BO-3.description: Reduce storage and indexing cost for embeddings/search workloads compared with the current Elastic-based approach.

BO-4.description: Achieve very low-latency retrieval over large document sets for downstream agent use.

BO-5.description: Validate vendor claims with real demos, benchmarks, comparisons, and hands-on proof before making decisions.

FR-1.description: Support document search over unstructured content provided by customers, including PDFs and other uploaded document types.

FR-2.description: Support use cases that combine structured and unstructured data in retrieval workflows.

FR-3.description: Support agent memory/context retrieval from conversation-derived documents.

FR-4.description: Support retrieval and re-ranking so relevant results can be surfaced to agents.

FR-5.description: Handle large-scale vector retrieval across approximately one million documents in a single index.

FR-6.description: Support a POV/demo workflow where users can upload documents during the session and ask questions against them.

FR-7.description: Demonstrate multiple chunking strategies for document processing, including fixed-length, recursive, semantic, and contextual chunking.

FR-8.description: Support isolated per-customer SaaS deployments in addition to some multi-tenant services.

FR-9.description: Support tagging or access association at the document level for context records tied to users and tenants.

AI-1.description: Provide vector search capabilities for unstructured document retrieval.

AI-2.description: Enable embeddings generation and retrieval workflows for customer documents.

AI-3.description: Support PDF/document ingestion where users may upload unpredictable document types and still expect useful retrieval outcomes.

AI-4.description: Support retrieval accuracy benchmarking using customer-provided questions/ground truth.

AI-5.description: Evaluate retrieval quality using top-k based measures up to top 20.

AI-6.description: Compare retrieval precision, recall, and latency during the evaluation.

AI-7.description: Potentially support multimodal retrieval in the future, but it is not part of the requested benchmark flow for the next demo.

AI-8.description: Support agent conversation/session data as a backend database use case.

SC-1.description: Show that document search works well on customer-like documents uploaded during the demo.

SC-2.description: Demonstrate retrieval at the right latency for the document-search use case.

SC-3.description: Provide side-by-side comparison against a baseline or current system to determine whether there is significant difference.

SC-4.description: Demonstrate raw retrieval accuracy and speed using the same documents across systems.

SC-5.description: Evaluate precision, recall, and latency metrics in the demo/POV.

SC-6.description: Assess top-k retrieval quality at top 1, 5, 10, and 20.

SC-7.description: Validate that MongoDB/Voyage offers better results than the customer’s current or simple baseline approach rather than merely matching it.

SC-8.description: Potential future success criterion: support around 400-500 concurrent requests, though this is not the immediate focus of the POV.

INT-1.description: Integrate with or replace parts of the current Elastic/Elastic Cloud based search and embeddings workflow.

INT-2.description: Coexist with Postgres, which is currently used as the application database and for some metadata.

INT-3.description: Coexist with S3, which currently stores raw documents.

INT-4.description: Fit into environments that already use OpenSearch for some customer deployments/use cases.

INT-5.description: Work within a multi-cloud environment across AWS, GCP, and/or other clouds.

INT-6.description: Potentially align with Vertex AI-based session management already in use for agents.

INT-7.description: Support content originating from connectors such as Slack, Confluence, Jira, Google Sheets, CSVs, and PDFs.
